headline: 84 detained in raid on senior police officer’s rented house in Dhaka
summary: Detectives seized drugs and alcohol during a raid on a property owned by an additional DIG, who has since been placed on OSD.
details: Detectives detained 84 people, including 26 women, during a raid on a three-storey house in Police Housing-1, under Khilkhet Police Station, in Dhaka.
The Detective Branch (DB) acted on intelligence that the property was being used for overnight 'DJ parties, drug use and drug dealing'.
Officers seized cannabis, yaba, alcohol, and equipment used to consume drugs during the operation.
The house is owned by Abdullah Al Zahir, an additional deputy inspector general (ADDL DIG)L at Police Headquarters, who had rented it out via Airbnb.
Following the raid, Zahir was withdrawn from the Personal Management-2 branch at Police Headquarters and placed in the officer on special duty (OSD) pool.
Zahir told bdnews24.com that the courtyard was rented for events like birthday parties and Gaye Holud, and that he had strict rules against illegal activities.
The officer questioned whether landlords should be held responsible for crimes committed by tenants without their knowledge.
caption:
84 people detained, drugs seized—all at a house rented out by a senior police officer.

Detectives detained 84 people, including 26 women, during a raid on a three-storey house in Police Housing-1, under Khilkhet Police Station, in Dhaka.

The Detective Branch (DB) acted on intelligence that the property was being used for overnight 'DJ parties, drug use and drug dealing'.

Officers seized cannabis, yaba, alcohol, and equipment used to consume drugs during the operation.

The house is owned by Abdullah Al Zahir, an additional deputy inspector general (ADDL DIG)L at Police Headquarters, who had rented it out via Airbnb.

Following the raid, Zahir was withdrawn from the Personal Management-2 branch at Police Headquarters and placed in the officer on special duty (OSD) pool.

Zahir told bdnews24.com that the courtyard was rented for events like birthday parties and Gaye Holud, and that he had strict rules against illegal activities.

The officer questioned whether landlords should be held responsible for crimes committed by tenants without their knowledge.

headline_marked: Family in Tangail fear [[Sweety Akhtar executed in Saudi Arabia]]
headline: Family in Tangail fear Sweety Akhtar executed in Saudi Arabia
summary: A day labourer from Mirzapur is desperate for official confirmation after hearing reports that his daughter, who was imprisoned in Saudi Arabia, has been executed.
details: Fazal Mia, a day labourer from Nagar Chhawali village in Tangail's Mirzapur upazila, is waiting for official confirmation after reports that his daughter, Sweety Akhtar, was executed in Saudi Arabia.
Sweety had gone to Saudi Arabia nearly four years ago. Her father borrowed Tk 1.5 lakh to send her there for work.
After five months of working, Sweety informed her family that she had been imprisoned. She claimed she was framed following an argument with other female workers.
Despite being in jail, she remained in contact with her family, calling home roughly once a month. In her last call 15 days ago, she told her family she might be released in two months.
The family learned of the reported execution two days ago through unofficial channels. They have received no official notification from the Bangladesh government.
The Ministry of Foreign Affairs recently stated it had learned of the execution of two Bangladeshis in Saudi Arabia but could not confirm their identities.
Sweety's mother, Johura, is desperate for answers, stating she just wants her daughter back, whether she is alive or dead.
Local authorities in Mirzapur, including the Union Parishad chairman and Police Station Officer-in-Charge, have confirmed they have received no official information regarding Sweety's fate.
caption:
A father borrowed Tk 1.5 lakh to send his daughter to work in Saudi Arabia. Now, he is waiting for confirmation that she has been executed.

Fazal Mia, a day labourer from Nagar Chhawali village in Tangail's Mirzapur upazila, is waiting for official confirmation after reports that his daughter, Sweety Akhtar, was executed in Saudi Arabia.

Sweety had gone to Saudi Arabia nearly four years ago. Her father borrowed Tk 1.5 lakh to send her there for work.

After five months of working, Sweety informed her family that she had been imprisoned. She claimed she was framed following an argument with other female workers.

Despite being in jail, she remained in contact with her family, calling home roughly once a month. In her last call 15 days ago, she told her family she might be released in two months.

The family learned of the reported execution two days ago through unofficial channels. They have received no official notification from the Bangladesh government.

The Ministry of Foreign Affairs recently stated it had learned of the execution of two Bangladeshis in Saudi Arabia but could not confirm their identities.

Sweety's mother, Johura, is desperate for answers, stating she just wants her daughter back, whether she is alive or dead.

Local authorities in Mirzapur, including the Union Parishad chairman and Police Station Officer-in-Charge, have confirmed they have received no official information regarding Sweety's fate.
